title: Naturality of normalized scalar reduction boundaries
statement: Let A,B,A',B' be abelian categories with derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let exact additive functors R:B→A, R':B'→A', F:A→A', G:B→B' have an isomorphism ρ:R F≅G R'. Let L⊣D(R), L'⊣D(R') commute with shifts, and let a shift-compatible θ:L D(G)≅D(F) L' satisfy the derived mate-unit equation. Let S,S' be short exact sequences [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], let f:S'≅F(S), and choose H,Q in B and H',Q' in B', with h:H'≅GH and q:Q'≅GQ. Let i:RH→S.X₁ and i':R'H'→S'.X₁ give short exact multiplication sequences with final map n times the identity. Let p:S.X₃→RQ and p':S'.X₃→R'Q'. Suppose αF:L(S.X₃[0])≅Q[0] and αB:L(S.X₁[0])≅H[1], and primed versions, are normalized by the derived unit: αF has adjunct p[0], while αB has adjunct the canonical Kummer connecting morphism, using the canonical single and shift comparisons. Assume i' followed by f₁ equals R'(h) followed by ρ inverse and F(i), and f₃ followed by F(p) equals p' followed by R'(q) and ρ inverse. Then both α squares commute with θ, f, h and q. The boundaries b=αF inverse followed by L(δS) and αB[1], with the canonical [1][1]→[2] comparison, and b' satisfy D(G)(b) followed by the shift and single comparisons equals the single comparison followed by q inverse, b' and h[2].

proof.text: Prove that the derived square induced by ρ commutes with the canonical single-complex comparisons. Expand exact-functor factorization isomorphisms; the required complex equation is ρ naturality in degree zero and equality out of zero in other degrees. The shift version follows from shift compatibility.

The target adjunction is injective on morphisms. Apply it to the quotient identification square. The mate-unit equation and quotient-unit normalizations reduce it to the assumed equation for p and p' and naturality of the single comparison.

Apply the target adjunction to the Kummer identification square. The equation for i and i' defines a map between the image multiplication sequence and the primed multiplication sequence, with components ρ followed by R'(h inverse), f₁ inverse, f₁ inverse. Naturality of the canonical single triangle and exact preservation of its boundary give the required adjunct equality, including its sign.

The exact image of δS commutes with f by naturality of the short exact sequence triangle. Express b as a composition in shifted Hom. Functoriality of shifted composition, θ naturality, the two identification squares, and naturality of the shift-add isomorphism give the degree-two boundary square.

proof_origin.place: Paragraphs 4 and 5; explicit exact-adjunction comparison and canonical shifted boundary calculation.

theorem CategoryTheory.normalizedScalarBoundaryNaturality :
    let b := aF.inv ≫ (ShiftedHom.map hS.singleδ L).comp aB.hom (show (1 : ℤ) + 1 = 2 from rfl)
    let b' := aF'.inv ≫ (ShiftedHom.map hS'.singleδ L').comp aB'.hom
      (show (1 : ℤ) + 1 = 2 from rfl)
    (G.mapDerivedCategory.map aF.hom ≫ (G.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app Q =
      θ.hom.app ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0).obj S.X₃) ≫
        L'.map ((F.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app S.X₃) ≫
        L'.map ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A' 0).map f.inv.τ₃) ≫ aF'.hom ≫
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor B' 0).map q.hom) ∧
    (G.mapDerivedCategory.map aB.hom ≫
        (G.mapDerivedCategory.commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).hom.app
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor B 0).obj H) ≫
        ((G.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app H)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' =
      θ.hom.app ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0).obj S.X₁) ≫
        L'.map ((F.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app S.X₁) ≫
        L'.map ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A' 0).map f.inv.τ₁) ≫ aB'.hom ≫
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor B' 0).map h.hom)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧') ∧
    (ShiftedHom.map b G.mapDerivedCategory ≫
        ((G.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app H)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧' =
      (G.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor 0).hom.app Q ≫
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor B' 0).map q.inv ≫ b' ≫
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor B' 0).map h.hom)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧')
